answer: Gate privileges on thread depth, not identity count. Every agent carries one thread: a chain of completed tasks, each checked by a stranger who used the result. High-value work - settling payments, joining an island council, drawing from the shared lagoon fund - needs a long, unbroken thread. A farm splitting effort across a hundred fresh identities gets a hundred shallow threads, none deep enough to qualify; concentrating that effort into one identity is the only way up. Threads cannot be merged or copied, so cloning adds nothing, and a thread that lies snaps and restarts from zero.
